trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival – Flight TP lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Aerobus or Metro (Linha Vermelha) from Lisbon Airport to the city centre for €1.85–€2.15. Check in at Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour – Head to the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré (reachable by Metro or tram). Sample the best of Portuguese cuisine: try a bifana (pork sandwich), fresh seafood, and local wines. Graze through multiple stalls to keep costs down by sharing smaller portions.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Bairro Alto and Chiado neighbourhoods. Explore the charming streets, pop into local tascas, and enjoy the lively atmosphere. End the night with a glass of Ginjinha (cherry liqueur) at a street-side kiosk for under €2.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a pastel de nata and coffee at the airport café for ~€2–3 before landing.
meals.lunch: Time Out Market – budget €10–15 by mixing smaller dishes from different vendors.
meals.dinner: Tasca do Chico or a local tasca in Bairro Alto – look for the 'prato do dia' (dish of the day) for €7–10 including bread and drink.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 24-hour Viva Viagem transport card (€0.50 card + top-up) for unlimited Metro/bus/tram travel. Keep your first afternoon light as jet lag may set in. The Time Out Market is open until midnight so timing is flexible.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Alfama – Lisbon's oldest and most historic neighbourhood. Walk up to the Castelo de São Jorge (€15 entry, or admire it from outside for free). Wander the narrow medieval alleyways, visit the Miradouro da Graça viewpoint for panoramic city views, and soak in the history of Moorish Lisbon.
day_by_day.afternoon: National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) – Take a short bus or tram ride to this world-class museum housed in a stunning 16th-century convent. Entry is €5 (reduced/free on Sunday mornings). Discover Portugal's iconic azulejo tile tradition spanning 500 years of artistry and history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Alfama for an authentic Fado experience. Many small tascas offer free Fado performances in the evening – look for spots on Rua de São João da Praça. Enjoy dinner while listening to Portugal's soulful national music.

meals.breakfast: Café near Lisbon City Stay – coffee and a pastel de nata for €1.50–2.50. Ask locals for the nearest padaria (bakery).
meals.lunch: Mercado de Santa Clara or a local café in Alfama – grilled sardines or caldo verde soup for €5–8.
meals.dinner: Local tasca in Alfama with Fado – prato do dia (bacalhau à brás or grilled chicken) for €8–12 including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes – Alfama involves steep cobblestone hills. The National Tile Museum is closed on Mondays. Sunday morning entry to the museum is free before 2pm, so consider swapping to Sunday if preferred.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Landmarks – Take Tram 15E or Bus 728 from Praça do Comércio to Belém (~20 min, €2). Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery (€10 entry, free on Sunday mornings before 14:00 – arrive early!). Marvel at the extraordinary Manueline Gothic architecture built to celebrate Portugal's Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Belém – Walk along the riverside to the iconic Tower of Belém (€6 entry). Explore the nearby Monument to the Discoveries (€6 or admire from outside for free). Stroll the waterfront gardens and enjoy the scenic views of the Tagus River and the 25 de Abril Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Baixa-Chiado. Visit Praça do Comércio at golden hour for stunning riverside views. Walk up to Miradouro de Santa Catarina (free) to watch the sunset over the Tagus with locals.

meals.breakfast: Pastéis de Belém – the original pastel de nata bakery (open since 1837). Try 2–3 pastéis for ~€2.50. This is a must-do Lisbon experience!
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local supermercado (Pingo Doce or Lidl) near Belém – grab bread, cheese, local charcuterie, and fruit for €4–6.
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Ramiro alternative – try Solar dos Presuntos or a cervejaria in Baixa for petiscos (Portuguese tapas) shared between travellers for €8–12 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Arriving at Jerónimos Monastery before 10:00 on Sunday ensures free entry and smaller crowds. The Belém area is spread out but walkable along the riverside. Combine Tram 15E with walking to save on transport costs.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Mouraria and Intendente – Lisbon's multicultural heart and one of the city's oldest neighbourhoods. Visit the colourful Intendente Square (Largo do Intendente), browse the local market stalls, and discover street art and azulejo-decorated buildings. This is an authentic, tourist-light experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Parque das Nações (Park of Nations) – Take the Metro (Linha Vermelha) to Oriente station. Explore this modern riverside district built for Expo '98. Walk along the Tagus promenade, see the futuristic Oriente Station (free to admire), and visit the Oceanarium exterior or gardens. The area is great for a relaxed walk without spending much.
day_by_day.evening: LX Factory – Take a bus or Uber back to Alcântara. Explore this hip creative hub in a repurposed 19th-century industrial complex. Browse independent shops, street art, and food stalls. Monday is quieter than weekends but many venues are still open.

meals.breakfast: Café Nicola or any local café in Baixa – galão (milky coffee) and toast with butter and jam for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Mouraria neighbourhood – try a prato do dia at a local tasca for €6–9. Look for restaurants frequented by locals rather than tourists.
meals.dinner: LX Factory restaurants – Buddha Lounge or A Taberna da Rua das Flores nearby offer affordable dinner options for €10–14. Or grab street food at LX Factory for €6–8.

day_by_day.notes: Monday is when some museums are closed (including the National Tile Museum), so this day is designed around free outdoor exploration. Parque das Nações is great for budget travellers as most enjoyment is free along the waterfront.

day_by_day.morning: Sintra Day Trip (optional budget adventure) – Take the train from Rossio Station to Sintra (€2.35 each way, ~40 min). Explore the UNESCO World Heritage town on foot. Walk up to the colourful Pena Palace exterior and gardens (€14 entry or admire from the free viewpoint on the hill) and visit the free historic village centre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lisbon by mid-afternoon. Visit the free Miradouro do Parque Eduardo VII for sweeping city views. Walk down the grand Avenida da Liberdade, window-shopping Lisbon's elegant boulevard. Stop at the historic Praça dos Restauradores.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Lisbon – Return to your favourite neighbourhood for a farewell dinner. Visit a traditional cervejaria or tasca. Pick up souvenirs at local shops: tinned fish (conservas), ginjinha, or azulejo tiles are affordable and authentic gifts.

meals.breakfast: Café A Brasileira in Chiado (historic café since 1905) – coffee and pastel for €3–4. Sit outside for the atmosphere.
meals.lunch: Sintra village – try a queijada de Sintra (local pastry, €1–2 each) and a sandwich from a local café for €4–6 total.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a traditional tasca in Bairro Alto or Alfama – order bacalhau (salt cod), grilled sardines, or carne de porco à alentejana with house wine for €10–15. Toast with a local Vinho Verde!

day_by_day.notes: For Sintra, buy a round-trip train ticket at Rossio Station early to avoid queues. If skipping Sintra, use the morning for any missed Lisbon sights or a relaxed café morning. Keep €10–15 aside for transport to the airport on departure day. Overall daily budget target: €40–60 per day including accommodation, food, transport, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Lisbon, Portugal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use the morning flight time to rest and prepare.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line) to central Lisbon and check in to Lisbon City Stay. Once settled, take a leisurely self-guided stroll through Baixa-Chiado, Lisbon's elegant downtown grid, exploring Praça do Comércio by the Tagus River and the famous Rua Augusta pedestrian street to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show — explore the medieval alleyways of Lisbon's oldest neighborhood with a guide, then settle in for an authentic Fado performance, the soulful music born in these very streets.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy snacks or a light meal on the plane or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the hotel after check-in — try A Cevicheria or a local tasca (tavern) in Chiado for a Portuguese sandwich (bifana) and a glass of wine.
meals.dinner: Dinner is typically included or paired with the Fado show experience in Alfama. Expect traditional dishes like bacalhau à brás (salted cod) or caldo verde soup.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Pack comfortable walking shoes as Alfama's cobblestone hills can be steep. Book the Fado show in advance as spots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) — spend 2–3 hours discovering Portugal's iconic blue-and-white azulejo tile tradition housed in a breathtaking 16th-century convent. The panoramic tile panel of pre-earthquake Lisbon is unmissable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — spend a culinary afternoon at this iconic food hall in Cais do Sodré, sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine including petiscos (small bites), grilled seafood, pastéis de nata, and local wines from top Lisbon chefs.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the trendy LX Factory, a repurposed industrial complex in Alcântara, browsing shops, street art, and enjoying a relaxed dinner at one of its eclectic restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Start at a traditional Lisbon café near the hotel — try a galão (milky espresso) and a pastel de nata or a tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese sandwich).
meals.lunch: Lunch is covered by the Time Out Market food tour — budget €15–25 for generous tastings across multiple stalls.
meals.dinner: Dine at LX Factory — try O Corvo or another mid-range spot for grilled fish, pork cheeks (bochechas de porco), and local Alentejo wine. Budget €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Tile Museum is a short Uber or bus ride from central Lisbon. Arrive at Time Out Market mid-afternoon to avoid peak crowds. LX Factory has a popular Sunday market if your visit falls on a weekend.

day_by_day.morning: Take a 20-minute tram or bus ride to Belém for the Belém Historical Landmarks & Pastéis de Belém experience — visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a masterpiece of Manueline Gothic architecture, and the iconic Tower of Belém along the Tagus riverfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery (open since 1837) for the original custard tarts dusted with cinnamon. Then explore the Monument to the Discoveries and stroll along the riverside promenade. Return to the city center and visit the Carmo Archaeological Museum in Chiado, a roofless neo-Gothic church destroyed in the 1755 earthquake.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Bairro Alto neighborhood for dinner and evening drinks — this hilltop district comes alive at night with restaurants, wine bars, and local nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Eat near the hotel before heading to Belém — a café com leite and a croissant or yogurt at a neighborhood pastelaria.
meals.lunch: Eat near Belém — try Solar dos Presuntos or a riverside café for grilled sardines, piri-piri chicken, or a seafood rice dish. Budget €15–20.
meals.dinner: Dine in Bairro Alto at Taberna da Rua das Flores or a similar mid-range tasca for traditional petiscos and Portuguese wine. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Jerónimos Monastery tickets online in advance to skip the queue. Arrive in Belém by 9:30 AM to beat tour groups. Wear layers — the Tagus riverside can be breezy even in May.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Mouraria Food & History Walking Tour — explore Lisbon's oldest Moorish quarter and the birthplace of Fado with a small-group guide. Discover hidden squares, ancient mosques-turned-churches, and taste local street food including bifanas, ginjinha (cherry liqueur), and artisanal cheeses.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, visit the São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge) perched above Mouraria for sweeping panoramic views over Lisbon's rooftops and the Tagus River. Explore the castle ramparts and the small archaeological museum within.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Intendente neighborhood — once rough, now one of Lisbon's most vibrant multicultural districts — for dinner at a local restaurant celebrating Portuguese-African fusion cuisine, a nod to Lisbon's rich colonial history.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the Mouraria meeting point area — a local café serving tostas and espresso before the tour begins.
meals.lunch: Lunch is integrated into the Mouraria Food & History Walking Tour with multiple tastings included. Budget €5–10 for extra snacks.
meals.dinner: Dine in Intendente — try Tasca do Chico or a neighborhood restaurant for grilled fish, cataplana (seafood stew), or African-influenced piri-piri dishes. Budget €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Mouraria is hilly and the cobblestones can be uneven — wear sturdy shoes. The walking tour typically lasts 3 hours. São Jorge Castle is a 10-minute uphill walk from Mouraria — tuk-tuks are available if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Sintra (40 minutes by train from Rossio Station) — explore the fairy-tale Pena Palace perched on a hilltop, stroll through the lush UNESCO-listed Cultural Landscape, and visit the Moorish Castle ruins for incredible views over the Atlantic coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lisbon by early afternoon. Spend your last hours in the Príncipe Real neighborhood — browse its antique shops, visit the Jardim do Príncipe Real garden, and pick up artisanal souvenirs like azulejo tiles, local wine, or tinned Portuguese sardines.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely farewell dinner in Chiado or Cais do Sodré — splurge slightly on your last night with a memorable meal at a well-regarded Portuguese restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near Rossio Station before catching the Sintra train — a pastelaria with espresso, pastéis de nata, and fresh orange juice.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sintra village — try Tascantiga or a local café for a sandwich, soup, and queijadas de Sintra (local almond pastries). Budget €12–18.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Cervejaria Ramiro (seafood) or Taberna Albricoque in Cais do Sodré for a memorable final meal featuring grilled tiger prawns, percebes (barnacles), and vinho verde. Budget €35–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Buy Sintra train tickets the night before or use the Navegante transit card to avoid morning queues at Rossio. Sintra can be crowded — aim to be at Pena Palace by 9:30 AM. Return to Lisbon by 14:00 to allow time for afternoon exploration and a relaxed last evening.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Lisbon, Portugal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.description: Explore the oldest neighborhood in Lisbon on a guided walking tour through narrow medieval alleyways, visiting São Jorge Castle and the Sé Cathedral. End the evening at a traditional Fado house for an authentic Portuguese music performance paired with local wine.

experiences.name: National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo)
experiences.description: Discover Portugal's iconic azulejo tile tradition at this world-class museum housed in a stunning 16th-century convent. Explore over 500 years of decorative tile art, including a remarkable 75-foot panoramic tile panel depicting pre-earthquake Lisbon from 1755, offering a unique window into the city's history.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer from Humberto Delgado Airport to Lisbon City Stay hotel via luxury chauffeur service. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon stroll through the Chiado and Baixa districts near the hotel. Explore the elegant Praça do Comércio waterfront square, browse the iconic Livraria Bertrand (world's oldest operating bookshop), and soak in your first impressions of Lisbon's grand Pombaline architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show — Join an intimate guided evening walk through Lisbon's oldest medieval neighbourhood, winding through cobblestone alleys, past ancient Moorish walls, and up to panoramic miradouros. The tour culminates in an authentic Fado dinner show at a traditional casa de fado, where soulful Portuguese music accompanies a curated multi-course meal.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival. Enjoy a welcome amenity at the hotel upon check-in.
meals.lunch: Light late lunch at Café Lisboa inside the São Carlos National Theatre — elegant Portuguese snacks, petiscos, and fine wines in a beautifully restored setting.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Fado Show experience in Alfama — expect traditional dishes such as bacalhau à brás, caldo verde, and pastéis de nata paired with regional wines.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm Fado Show reservation ahead of time as top venues book out quickly. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for Alfama's steep cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Landmarks & Pastéis de Belém — Begin the morning with a private guided visit to the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline Gothic architecture dating to 1502. Marvel at the ornate cloisters and the tomb of Vasco da Gama. Then walk to the iconic Tower of Belém standing sentinel on the Tagus River. Conclude with the quintessential Lisbon ritual: warm, custard-fresh pastéis de nata at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery, operating since 1837.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the MAAT — Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology, a striking contemporary museum on the Belém waterfront with curated exhibitions blending art, science, and culture. Alternatively, explore the Museu de Marinha (Maritime Museum) within the Jerónimos complex for deeper historical immersion. Return to the hotel for a mid-afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a Michelin-starred restaurant in the Belém or Estrela area. Recommended: Feitoria (1 Michelin star) at Altis Belém Hotel, offering a refined tasting menu celebrating Portuguese seasonal produce with stunning Tagus River views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — full Portuguese spread including fresh bread, local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh fruit, and galão coffee.
meals.lunch: Pastéis de Belém for pastries, followed by a sit-down lunch at Taberna do Mercado or a riverside café in Belém — fresh grilled fish, açorda, and chilled Vinho Verde.
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred tasting menu at Feitoria — 8 to 10 courses with optional wine pairing featuring Douro, Alentejo, and Dão regional selections.

day_by_day.notes: Book Feitoria well in advance — it is one of Lisbon's most sought-after fine dining experiences. A private driver or taxi is recommended for the Belém day trip (~6 km from central Lisbon).

day_by_day.morning: National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) — Spend a rich morning at one of Lisbon's most extraordinary cultural institutions, housed in a stunning 16th-century convent. Trace five centuries of Portuguese azulejo tile art, from Moorish geometric patterns to Baroque masterpieces, including the magnificent 23-metre panoramic tile panel depicting pre-earthquake Lisbon. The museum's gilded Baroque chapel is not to be missed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mouraria Food & History Walking Tour — Join a small-group guided tour through Mouraria, Lisbon's ancient Moorish quarter and the birthplace of Fado. Discover hidden patios, Moorish archways, and centuries-old history while sampling authentic neighbourhood flavours — including artisanal cheeses, cured meats, traditional sweets, and local wines — at family-run tascos and specialty food shops.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar with panoramic city views. Recommended: TOPO Martim Moniz or Park Bar (atop a multi-storey car park in Bairro Alto) for golden-hour Tagus vistas. Follow with dinner at a premium contemporary Portuguese restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel. Alternatively, visit A Padaria Portuguesa for freshly baked breads, croissants, and espresso in a charming local setting.
meals.lunch: Included within the Mouraria Food & History Walking Tour — a progressive tasting experience across multiple neighbourhood stops.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alma (1 Michelin star, Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa) in Chiado — sophisticated modern Portuguese cuisine with an exceptional wine list in an intimate, beautifully designed space.

day_by_day.notes: The Tile Museum is closed on Mondays — Sunday is ideal. Mouraria tour involves moderate walking on uneven terrain; wear comfortable shoes. Alma reservations should be made several weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to Sintra — hire a private driver and guide for a morning visit to the UNESCO World Heritage fairy-tale town of Sintra, just 40 minutes from Lisbon. Explore the extravagant Palácio Nacional da Pena perched dramatically above the clouds, and stroll through the romantic gardens of Quinta da Regaleira with its mystical initiation wells and Masonic symbolism.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — Return to Lisbon and spend a curated culinary afternoon at the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré. Sample the best of Portuguese cuisine across carefully selected stalls: from bifanas and prego sandwiches to fresh seafood, ginjinha, artisan cheese boards, and contemporary interpretations of classic dishes — all under one spectacular roof.
day_by_day.evening: Leisurely evening in the Príncipe Real neighbourhood — browse the antique shops and design boutiques, visit the weekend garden market, and enjoy aperitivo-style drinks at a chic wine bar. Recommended: By the Wine (José Maria da Fonseca wine bar) for an exceptional curated selection of Portuguese wines by the glass.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — full service.
meals.lunch: Light snacks and pastries in Sintra — try the local travesseiros (almond and egg cream pastries) and queijadas at Piriquita, a Sintra institution since 1862.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bairro do Avillez (Chef José Avillez) in Chiado — a vibrant multi-concept space offering refined petiscos and contemporary Portuguese dishes in a lively, design-forward setting.

day_by_day.notes: Sintra can be crowded on weekends; a Monday visit with a private guide ensures priority access and a more exclusive experience. Bring a light layer as Sintra is cooler and mistier than Lisbon. Confirm private driver booking the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — sleep in and enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Afterward, take a private guided visit to the São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge), the ancient Moorish citadel crowning Lisbon's highest hill. Enjoy sweeping 360-degree views over the city, the Tagus estuary, and the distant Serra de Sintra, with expert historical commentary on Lisbon's Phoenician, Roman, Moorish, and medieval past.
day_by_day.afternoon: Curated luxury shopping in Chiado and Príncipe Real — visit Luvaria Ulisses (world's smallest glove shop, founded 1925), Claus Porto for artisanal Portuguese soaps and perfumes, and Vista Alegre for exquisite Portuguese porcelain. Stop for a final galão and pastel de nata at Café A Brasileira, Lisbon's most iconic literary café on Rua Garrett. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Belcanto (2 Michelin stars, Chef José Avillez) — Lisbon's most celebrated fine dining restaurant in the heart of Chiado. An extraordinary tasting menu reimagining the soul of Portuguese culinary heritage through avant-garde technique, impeccable service, and a world-class wine cellar. The perfect final memory of Lisbon.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at the hotel — the finest spread of the trip to mark the final morning.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Solar dos Presuntos in Restauradores — a beloved Lisbon institution renowned for its traditional presunto (cured ham), bacalhau dishes, and warm hospitality since 1974.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell tasting menu at Belcanto (2 Michelin stars) — 10 to 12 courses with full wine pairing. Reserve the chef's table or private dining room for an ultra-exclusive experience.

day_by_day.notes: Belcanto is one of the hardest restaurant reservations in Portugal — book as early as possible, ideally months in advance. Arrange a private chauffeur for the airport transfer on departure day. Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if the flight departs late.

query: Lisbon city break, $2500 couple, food and history, 5 days, May 2027, from Boston
